index.note: Flow opens the room: what the campaign is and what it shows, then two chapters that are also the section titles (where the look came from and why, then the same three parts from a billboard to a lock screen); the closing ends on the texture and the barrel.
index.stand: A campaign for Hill Country Oakworks, a Texas whiskey barrel maker. | Sun-washed color and the silhouette of an oak show the land the barrels come from.

Every piece of the campaign.t: The campaign pulls from travel posters and old highway signs,
Every piece of the campaign.g: for a heritage look that stays clear of the Western cliché
li: Red, white, and blue | the palette had to say Texas without them.
The colors | orange and mustard do the color blocks and the wordmark, brick is the foreground hills, and teal is the sky.
The type | plain and utilitarian, with Greatdome for the display type and Avenir Next for everything else.

The same three parts hold.t: The same three parts hold from a billboard to a lock screen,
The same three parts hold.g: with each piece laying out the color blocks, silhouette, and type for its own size
p: The campaign had to look like a heritage brand at both sizes.

lines.The geometric shapes in the artwork: A distressed texture goes over the whole campaign. | The geometric shapes in the artwork echo a whiskey barrel.
